note: Short, neutral paraphrases of each party's publicly stated priorities for the 2026 Victorian state election, drawn from the parties' own websites and announcements. Deliberately paraphrased in a positive 'what the party supports' voice where possible, rather than 'what it opposes'. Not endorsements. Policies evolve — the party's own website is canonical. If a line misrepresents a position, treat the party site as authoritative.

positions.Labor: Continue delivering the Big Housing Build; focus on social and affordable housing supply; planning reform to unlock density near transport.
positions.Coalition: Streamline planning processes to speed private supply; prefers market-led density over mandated density-near-transport; emphasises first-home-buyer support.
positions.Greens: Large-scale public housing expansion; strengthened renters' rights (indefinite leases, rent caps); end to no-grounds evictions; levy on vacant properties.
positions.One Nation: Attributes housing pressure primarily to immigration-driven demand; proposes reducing migration intake as the main policy lever.

positions.Labor: Target 95% renewable electricity by 2035; State Electricity Commission expansion; offshore wind development; EV incentives.
positions.Coalition: Energy policy prioritising reliability and cost; supports gas as a transition fuel; cautious on renewables timelines.
positions.Greens: Faster coal exit (2030); community-owned renewables; expanded national parks; ending native-forest logging and new fossil-fuel projects.
positions.One Nation: Prioritises energy affordability and reliability; supports continued use of coal and gas; prefers an energy mix without binding net-zero timelines; cautious on large-scale wind development.

positions.Labor: Continued hospital infrastructure investment; women's health focus; mental health reforms post-Royal Commission; GP respite clinics.
positions.Coalition: Reduce elective-surgery waiting lists; shift resources from administration to frontline care; review hospital governance structures.
positions.Greens: Free dental in Medicare (state advocacy); fully funded public hospitals; mental-health care parity; harm-reduction drug policy.
positions.One Nation: Supports individual medical choice (including voluntary, non-mandated vaccination); raises concerns about health-workforce pressures from population growth.

positions.Labor: Free kinder for 3- and 4-year-olds; continued public school funding uplift; free TAFE courses; teacher recruitment incentives.
positions.Coalition: Back-to-basics curriculum; phonics-based literacy; stronger classroom discipline; expanded parental choice; parental opt-out from gender-identity content.
positions.Greens: Fully fund public schools to Gonski 100%; free TAFE and university; smaller class sizes; higher teacher pay.
positions.One Nation: Supports a focus on traditional academic subjects; expanded parental choice; religious freedom in schools; parental opt-out from gender-identity content.

positions.Labor: Suburban Rail Loop (SRL) delivery; Metro Tunnel operation; continued level crossing removals; EV charging rollout; airport rail commitment.
positions.Coalition: Considers SRL in current form too costly and wants it scaled back; prioritises road investment; faster regional rail; review of major-project procurement.
positions.Greens: Scrap SRL and divert funds to buses, trams, cycling, and local rail electrification; halt urban freeway expansion; free public transport.
positions.One Nation: Prioritises road and freight infrastructure; prefers road access without congestion charges; cautious on large rail megaprojects.

positions.Labor: Energy bill relief payments; continued power saving bonus; cheaper public-transport fares; targeted cost-of-living package in last budget.
positions.Coalition: Cut state taxes and levies (including Vic-specific property taxes); emphasis on cost-of-doing-business for small employers.
positions.Greens: Reduce costs of essentials via public ownership (energy, housing); dental in Medicare; rent caps; levies on large corporations.
positions.One Nation: Identifies immigration and current energy policy as primary drivers of inflation; proposes reducing migration and changing the energy mix.

positions.Labor: Youth justice reform combining diversion programs with stronger accountability; new stalking and family-violence laws; expanded police resources.
positions.Coalition: Tougher bail laws; mandatory minimum sentences for some offences; opposition to raising the age of criminal responsibility.
positions.Greens: Raise the age of criminal responsibility to 14; invest in diversion and treatment over incarceration; address drivers of crime.
positions.One Nation: Supports tougher sentencing (including mandatory minimums for some offences); expanded police resources; favours maintaining current drug laws.

positions.Labor: Continue the Treaty process via the First Peoples' Assembly; implement Yoorrook Justice Commission recommendations.
positions.Coalition: Withdrew support for a statewide Treaty framework in 2024; favours practical reconciliation initiatives over structural reforms.
positions.Greens: Full treaty implementation; truth-telling; return of Crown lands; backing Yoorrook recommendations in full.
positions.One Nation: Advocates formal equality in all public programs; prefers citizenship-based rather than Treaty-based or race-based policy frameworks.
